summary.intent: Update the codebase map documents (primarily CONCERNS.md) to reflect the work completed in phases 28-33, then sync with the latest main branch after Phase 33 was merged.
summary.outcome: CONCERNS.md and STRUCTURE.md were updated on a docs branch, with CONCERNS.md accurately reflecting all four major concerns from phases 28-33 as resolved and surfacing three new concerns. The final CONCERNS.md (233 lines) incorporated Phase 33's Windows async FilePointer fix after a stash/reset/re-run cycle.

repo: Phase 28 replaced 127 console.* calls with structured logger at apps/web/src/lib/logger.ts; only 2 files retain console.* calls
Phase 30 added Grafana Faro observability at apps/web/src/lib/faro.ts with sensitive data scrubbing, deployed via VITE_FARO_URL in staging CI
Phase 31 decomposed useSharedNavigation.ts (1199→378 lines) into 6 files and FileBrowser.tsx (964→362 lines)
Phase 32 resolved macOS FUSE FilePointer async blocking; Phase 33 resolved the Windows equivalent in crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/read_ops.rs using rt.spawn() channel patterns
registerFaroTransport() is defined but never called — logger.error/warn calls do not reach Faro
apps/web/src/lib/web3auth/hooks.ts retains 12 unguarded console.time/timeEnd calls not covered by Phase 28
19+ mutex lock().unwrap() sites exist in FUSE production code that can cause cascading panics on poisoned mutex
folder.service.ts (1059 lines) and bin.service.ts (971 lines) remain large but are considered cohesive enough to not warrant a concern entry
IPNS unenrollment is handled fire-and-forget by the SDK without persistence across tab closure

code.finding: 12 unguarded console.time/timeEnd calls surviving Phase 28 cleanup
registerFaroTransport() defined but never called, so logger errors don't reach Faro
Phase 32 converted FilePointer resolution to async via rt.spawn() channel patterns (macOS)
Phase 33 converted FilePointer resolution to async on Windows, mirroring macOS fix

workflow: The map-codebase workflow supports selective document updates — useful for targeted refreshes after known phase work without full remap
Mapper agents write documents directly and return only confirmations, keeping orchestrator context minimal

When divergent branches occur after a mapper commit, the correct recovery is: stash the planning doc changes, hard reset to origin/main, restore the stash, then re-run the mapper to pick up newly merged code
Running concerns analysis twice (before and after Phase 33 merge) was necessary because Phase 33 was merged to origin/main during the session

friction: git pull failed with 'divergent branches' error because a mapper commit had been made locally before pulling — required stash/reset/restore dance
Had to re-run the concerns mapper a second time after syncing with origin/main to capture Phase 33's Windows fix, duplicating ~7 minutes of agent work
